title: The wheel and the ruler

data.source: The flat rotor of MATHEMATICS.md R4 with fast correlated noise, 1500 runs per setting.

prediction: With a flat potential and fast noise the gaps between cuts follow the inverse Gaussian law, mean a/v and CV sqrt(2D/(v a)); a cut defined on the circle from either side would differ by the textbook two-sided exit formulas; the CV follows the noise and is not one fixed number.
baseline: First passage of Brownian motion with drift: the inverse Gaussian law (Schroedinger 1915, Wald 1947) and the two-sided exit formulas.
why: P1 and P3 held; P2 held in kind but missed its stated tolerance (see the numbers). R2 on the lifted line is the textbook first-passage problem, and its answer was already known. The spread of the gaps is set by the noise, so CRR gives no fixed number for it.
